content.text:
Fixed: emphasis inside a rejected reference link now renders, and your example produces exactly the CommonMark output. The spec suite (1789 tests) and the unit tests (45) all pass; `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.

**Cause.** Before tokenizing inline text, `inlineTokens` in `src/Lexer.ts` masks every `[text][ref]` with a defined ref so that `*`/`_` delimiters can't pair across a link boundary. When the tokenizer later rejects that link because its text holds another link, the brackets become plain text, but the mask was still hiding the delimiters inside. The emphasis scanner therefore never found a closer.

**Fix.** The masking now lives in a new `maskReflinks` method in `src/Lexer.ts`. For a reference link whose text contains a `[`, it checks whether the tokenizer would reject it. If so, it leaves the text visible and masks only the links that survive: the inner link and the trailing `[ref]`.

This covers `_`, `**`, `~~`, an inner reference link (example 533), and an emphasis opener that sits before the rejected link, as in `*a [b [c](/url) d*][ref]`.

**Tests.**
- Example 533 was flagged `shouldFail` in both `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`; I removed the flag since it now passes.
- I added `test/specs/new/em_in_rejected_reflink.md` and `.html` with the report's cases plus the variants above.

One cost to be aware of: the text of such a link is tokenized one extra time during masking. This only happens for reference links whose text contains a bracket.

Fixed: emphasis inside a rejected reference link now renders, and your example produces exactly the CommonMark output. The spec suite (1789 tests) and the unit tests (45) all pass; `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.

**Cause.** Before tokenizing inline text, `inlineTokens` in `src/Lexer.ts` masks every `[text][ref]` with a defined ref so that `*`/`_` delimiters can't pair across a link boundary. When the tokenizer later rejects that link because its text holds another link, the brackets become plain text, but the mask was still hiding the delimiters inside. The emphasis scanner therefore never found a closer.

**Fix.** The masking now lives in a new `maskReflinks` method in `src/Lexer.ts`. For a reference link whose text contains a `[`, it checks whether the tokenizer would reject it. If so, it leaves the text visible and masks only the links that survive: the inner link and the trailing `[ref]`.

This covers `_`, `**`, `~~`, an inner reference link (example 533), and an emphasis opener that sits before the rejected link, as in `*a [b [c](/url) d*][ref]`.

**Tests.**
- Example 533 was flagged `shouldFail` in both `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`; I removed the flag since it now passes.
- I added `test/specs/new/em_in_rejected_reflink.md` and `.html` with the report's cases plus the variants above.

One cost to be aware of: the text of such a link is tokenized one extra time during masking. This only happens for reference links whose text contains a bracket.
